PLANNING.detail:
Title: Hard Sorting Strategy Pattern Exercise

Intended changes:
- solution repository: modify `BubbleSort.performSort` to throw IllegalArgumentException when input is null before sorting
- solution repository: modify `MergeSort.performSort` to throw IllegalArgumentException when input is null before sorting
- solution repository: modify `Context.sort` to throw IllegalStateException if sortAlgorithm is null
- test repository: add test class `SortStrategyNullTest` with test method `testPerformSortNull` (test ID 1800) asserting IllegalArgumentException for null input on both BubbleSort and MergeSort
- test repository: add test class `ContextNoStrategyTest` with test method `testSortWithoutStrategy` (test ID 1801) asserting IllegalStateException when Context.sort() is called without a strategy
- test repository: add test class `PolicyEmptyListTest` with test method `testConfigureEmptyList` (test ID 1802) asserting that Policy.configure() selects BubbleSort for an empty date list

Invariants:
- the build tooling (Maven) and dependency set remain unchanged
- all original test case names and signatures stay identical unless explicitly listed in intendedChanges
- the template repository still compiles but fails all tests, including the newly added ones
- the solution repository passes all original tests and the newly added hardening tests
- no existing class, interface, or method names that are part of the teaching goal (SortStrategy, Context, Policy, BubbleSort, MergeSort) are renamed
- the number of original test cases stays the same; only additional tests are added

Problem statement:
In this exercise, we want to implement sorting algorithms and choose them based on runtime specific variables.

### Part 1: Sorting

First, we need to implement two sorting algorithms, in this case `MergeSort` and `BubbleSort`.

**You have the following tasks:**

1. [task][Implement Bubble Sort](<testid>1732</testid>)
Implement the method `performSort(List<Date>)` in the class `BubbleSort`. Make sure to follow the Bubble Sort algorithm exactly.

2. [task][Implement Merge Sort](<testid>1730</testid>)
Implement the method `performSort(List<Date>)` in the class `MergeSort`. Make sure to follow the Merge Sort algorithm exactly.

3. [task][Handle Null Input in SortStrategy](<testid>1800</testid>)
Ensure that `performSort(null)` throws an `IllegalArgumentException` for both sorting algorithms.

### Part 2: Strategy Pattern

We want the application to apply different algorithms for sorting a `List` of `Date` objects.
Use the strategy pattern to select the right sorting algorithm at runtime.

**You have the following tasks:**

1. [task][SortStrategy Interface](<testid>1734</testid>,<testid>1738</testid>)
Create a `SortStrategy` interface and adjust the sorting algorithms so that they implement this interface.

2. [task][Context Class](<testid>1733</testid>,<testid>1737</testid>)
Create and implement a `Context` class following the below class diagram.

3. [task][Context Policy](<testid>1736</testid>,<testid>1729</testid>,<testid>1739</testid>)
Create and implement a `Policy` class following the below class diagram with a simple configuration mechanism:

    1. [task][Select MergeSort](<testid>1731</testid>,<testid>1728</testid>)
    Select `MergeSort` when the List has more than 10 dates.

    2. [task][Select BubbleSort](<testid>1735</testid>,<testid>1727</testid>)
    Select `BubbleSort` when the List has less or equal 10 dates.

4. [task][Context without Strategy](<testid>1801</testid>)
Ensure that calling `Context.sort()` without a configured strategy throws an `IllegalStateException`.

5. [task][Policy with Empty List](<testid>1802</testid>)
Verify that `Policy.configure()` selects `BubbleSort` when the date list is empty.

6. Complete the `Client` class which demonstrates switching between two strategies at runtime.

}

class Policy {
  <color:testsColor(<testid>1739</testid>)>+configure()</color>
}

class Context {
  <color:testsColor(<testid>1733</testid>)>-dates: List<Date></color>
  <color:testsColor(<testid>1737</testid>)>+sort()</color>
}

interface SortStrategy {
  <color:testsColor(<testid>1738</testid>)>+performSort(List<Date>)</color>
}

class BubbleSort {
  <color:testsColor(<testid>1732</testid>)>+performSort(List<Date>)</color>
}

class MergeSort {
  <color:testsColor(<testid>1730</testid>)>+performSort(List<Date>)</color>
}

MergeSort -up-|> SortStrategy #testsColor(<testid>1731</testid>)
BubbleSort -up-|> SortStrategy #testsColor(<testid>1735</testid>)
Policy -right-> Context #testsColor(<testid>1729</testid>): context
Context -right-> SortStrategy #testsColor(<testid>1733</testid>): sortAlgorithm
Client .down.> Policy
Client .down.> Context

hide empty fields
hide empty methods

@enduml

### Part 3: Optional Challenges

(These are not tested)

1. Create a new class `QuickSort` that implements `SortStrategy` and implement the Quick Sort algorithm.

2. Make the method `performSort(List<Dates>)` generic, so that other objects can also be sorted by the same method.
   **Hint:** Have a look at Java Generics and the interface `Comparable`.

3. Think about a useful decision in `Policy` when to use the new `QuickSort` algorithm.
